_README: What each QPS code means, in the coders' own words.
Optional. The classifiers learn from examples and read none of this. It
exists for the language model, which is consulted only on the records the
classifiers cannot code — and those are overwhelmingly the rare codes,
where there are too few examples to learn from but a definition is
exactly as good as it is for a common code.
Five Process categories are currently never predicted correctly because
they appear once or twice in three years of records. A definition is the
only thing that can reach them.
Format: field name -> code (exactly as it appears in the exports) -> what
it means. Fill in what the team has; partial coverage is useful, and
`python -m src.reports sufficiency` states how much of the taxonomy is
covered. Fields left out are simply not described to the model.
The examples below are placeholders taken from the code names themselves.
They are NOT the team's definitions and should be replaced.
Ask the TIR team for the QPS code dictionary.
